findings: 2026-11-06: drafted for Mathematics 12 Unit 6 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: In Example 10 the book prints (x - 2)^{2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = \pm 2. A perfect square equal to zero gives only one (repeated) root: (x - 2)^{2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = 2. The value x = -2 does not satisfy x^{2} - 4x + 4 = 0 (it gives 16). The book's next line correctly uses the single point P(2, -2), so the answer is unchanged.
